title: Persona-driven component priority matrix + accessibility findings (wireframe notes)
body:
Summary:
This doc captures a lightweight persona-driven prioritization matrix for console components plus accessibility findings from the Feb wireframe pass. Purpose is pragmatic: align PM, design, and frontend on which components to tighten for the next sprint (focus: rollout flows + model selection modal), and call out immediate a11y fixes vs. larger refactors.

Context:
- Deliverable for Q2 rollout polish: make the new model selection + route configuration flows usable for two main personas while meeting baseline WCAG guidance.
- Past audits flagged color contrast, focus management, and insufficient semantic structure on modals. We iterated wireframes 2026-02-05; this doc synthesizes feedback and proposes priorities.
- Audience: product designers, frontend engineers, QA, accessibility reviewer.

Personas considered (short):
- Platform Engineer (P1): heavy keyboard-driven workflows, config-first, cares about speed and traceability. Needs keyboard focus order, clear affordances, and copy that surfaces connection state.
- Product Developer (P2): prototyping model choices, toggles, quick preview; uses mouse and keyboard, expects inline validation and helpful defaults.
- Solutions Engineer (P3): demos and customer-facing setup, needs predictable visuals and safe fallbacks for demos (no accidental data leaks).

Priority Matrix (component x persona) — quick view (R = required, H = high, M = medium, L = low):
- Model selection modal: P1=R, P2=H, P3=H => Priority: P0 (ship-critical)
- Route config form (advanced options collapsed): P1=H, P2=M, P3=H => Priority: P1
- Token usage bar / cost estimator: P1=M, P2=H, P3=L => Priority: P1
- Batch size / timeout controls: P1=H, P2=L, P3=M => Priority: P1
- Inline error toasts vs. field-level errors: P1=R, P2=H, P3=M => Priority: P0
- Accessible color tokens & palette mapping: P1=R, P2=M, P3=M => Priority: P0

Wireframe notes (component-level — refs to screens in Sketch/figma):
1) Model selection modal (wireframe v3):
   - Flow: open -> quick-filter search -> recommended models -> details panel -> confirm.
   - Observations: the details panel currently traps focus (close button not reachable by tab from last interactive element). On small screens the panel visually overlaps bottom action buttons.
   - Wireframe changes suggested: ensure a visible focusable close control in the header, move confirmation actions into a sticky footer region (separate from details panel). Add aria-labelledby on modal wrapper and aria-modal="true". Provide escape key behavior doc note.
   - UX questions: should selecting a model always show quantization/latency badges? or toggle by user (compact vs. detailed)?

2) Route config (single page with advanced section):
   - Observations: advanced section collapse is purely visual; screen readers still expose content in order that confuses keyboard users. Need aria-expanded plumbing and correct region roles.
   - Wireframe suggestion: switch to <details> pattern or explicit button that toggles a region with aria-controls and aria-expanded set. Use aria-live polite to announce state change.

3) Token usage bar:
   - Observations: color-only indicator with thin stroke; insufficient contrast for low-vision. Tooltip only appears on hover.
   - Suggested: add textual percentage inside the bar, accept reduced reliance on color. Add role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax and an offscreen label. Make tooltip accessible via focus.

Accessibility findings (concrete):
- Focus order issues: several modals and side-panels fail to maintain logical tab sequence. Repro steps: open model modal -> tab through details -> shift-tab from heading doesn't land on close control. Likely due to stacking of portal nodes.
- Inconsistent keyboard affordances: some chips/tags are clickable via mouse but not keyboard. Ensure buttons are real <button> elements or have tabindex=0+key handlers (prefer native controls).
- Color contrast: token palette mapping shows primary actions at 3.8:1 on hover states; target >=4.5:1 for body text and >=3:1 for UI components but we prefer 4.5. Action: update elevated button token to darker shade or increase weight.
- Screen reader semantics: panels lack region/landmark roles; modals missing aria-modal and labelledby.
- Live region usage: inline validation uses visual red highlight but no aria-live announcements. Add aria-live polite messaging for inline validation failures.
- Motion and reduced-motion setting: several microinteractions (focus ring fade, fly-in panels) have no respect for prefers-reduced-motion.

Low-effort wins (can be done in a single sprint):
- Make all modal close controls keyboard-focusable and add aria-modal + aria-labelledby (owner: Marcus Li, frontend).
- Add aria-expanded/aria-controls to collapsible advanced sections (owner: Priya).
- Convert clickable chips to <button> with accessible labels; include title attr for tooltips (owner: Diego).
- Expose token usage as text and add role=progressbar (owner: Ellen / frontend).
- Fix contrast for primary elevated button hover state (owner: design tokens).

Larger investments (Q2 planning):
- Rework portal stacking and focus-trap utility to ensure consistent focus order across nested overlays — may impact infrastructure and routing of portals. (Estimate: 2–3 sprints)
- Component library-level a11y test harness + axe integration in CI for console (fail build on regressions). (Estimate: 1 sprint setup + maintenance)
- Accessibility QA run with screen reader (NVDA/Mac VoiceOver) for core flows: signup -> create route -> run demo. (Cross-team effort)

Edge cases & known risks:
- Legacy embedded pages (internal admin) use older token palette; need migration guide to avoid visual regressions in customer demos.
- Private deployment styling: customers may inject CSS; recommend built-in forced-high-contrast token option for Console Private installs.

Unresolved questions (for triage):
- Do we prefer a compact model list (no badges) with an optional details flyout, or always show badges for transparency? Impact on cognitive load and scanning speed. Tagged for PM decision: CONFLUENCE-1234#decision.
- Should the progress bar be persistent on small screens or collapse into an icon+popover? We need mobile screenshots and usage metrics (ask analytics).

Next steps / owners / timeline:
- This sprint (Mar 1–14): implement low-effort wins and ship fix PRs. Owners assigned above.
- Mar 15–Apr 1: prototype focus-trap rework + run screen reader QA for model flow.
- Apr planning: prioritize CI axe integration and component-level tests.

Sketch & wireframe references (internal):
- figma: console -> model-selection v3 (frame id: 0:8492)
- figma: route-config v2 (frame id: 0:9021)
- local sketches: /design/temp/persona-model-matrix-02-06.pdf

Notes to self / rough todos:
- Coordinate with infra on portal node ownership — might need new global portal root for overlays.
- Add unit test checklist for a11y for each component: role semantics, keyboard behaviour, contrast token check, motion preference respect.
- Slack thread: #console-ui a11y flagged on 2026-02-18 — link to JIRA-RT-879 for tracking.

Appendix: quick checklist for QA run (short):
- Keyboard-only navigation through model modal (tab order, shift-tab).
- Screen reader announce sequence on open/close.
- Validate aria-expanded toggles on advanced sections.
- Contrast audit for 4 primary tokens on light/dark theme.
- Prefers-reduced-motion: toggle and verify overlay transitions are disabled.

End — comments welcome. Add any extra pain points, I'll fold into the matrix and reprioritize next grooming session.
